questions.title: Your first query
questions.question: The shop keeps its catalogue in a table called products. Show every column and every row of it.
questions.hint: SELECT * means "all columns". Then say which table with FROM.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT * FROM products;

questions.title: Pick your columns
questions.question: The marketing team only needs product names and prices. Show the name and price of every product, in that order.
questions.hint: List the columns you want after SELECT, separated by a comma.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT name, price FROM products;

questions.title: Calculate a column
questions.question: Show each product name and its price including 18% tax, rounded to 2 decimal places. Name the second column price_with_tax.
questions.hint: You can do maths in SELECT: price * 1.18. Wrap it in ROUND(..., 2) and give it a name with AS.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT name, ROUND(price * 1.18, 2) AS price_with_tax FROM products;

questions.title: No duplicates
questions.question: Which product categories does the shop sell? Show each category once.
questions.hint: SELECT DISTINCT removes duplicate rows from the result.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT DISTINCT category FROM products;

questions.title: Filter by text
questions.question: Show the name and city of every customer based in India.
questions.hint: Text values go in single quotes: WHERE country = 'India'.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, city TEXT NOT NULL, country TEXT NOT NULL, signup_date TEXT NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT name, city FROM customers WHERE country = 'India';

questions.title: Filter by number
questions.question: Which products cost more than 50? Show their name and price.
questions.hint: Numbers need no quotes. Use the > operator.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE price > 50;

questions.title: Two conditions
questions.question: Finance wants big orders that have already arrived. Show the id and total of orders with status 'delivered' and a total above 100.
questions.hint: Join two conditions with AND. Both must be true for a row to stay.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT id, total FROM orders WHERE status = 'delivered' AND total > 100;

questions.title: A date range
questions.question: Show the id and order_date of all orders placed from 1 February 2024 to 31 March 2024, including both days. Dates are stored as text like 2024-02-14.
questions.hint: BETWEEN includes both ends: WHERE order_date BETWEEN '2024-02-01' AND '2024-03-31'.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT id, order_date FROM orders WHERE order_date BETWEEN '2024-02-01' AND '2024-03-31';

questions.title: Missing values
questions.question: Some customers never gave us an email address. Show the name of every customer whose email is missing.
questions.hint: A missing value is NULL, and NULL never equals anything. Use IS NULL, not = NULL.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, city TEXT NOT NULL, country TEXT NOT NULL, signup_date TEXT NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE email IS NULL;

questions.title: Most expensive first
questions.question: Show the name and price of every product, from the most expensive to the cheapest.
questions.hint: ORDER BY price sorts low to high. Add DESC to flip it.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC;

questions.title: Sort by two columns
questions.question: Show each employee's name, department and salary. Sort by department A to Z, and within each department put the highest salary first.
questions.hint: ORDER BY takes a list: ORDER BY department, salary DESC. The second column only breaks ties in the first.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, department TEXT NOT NULL, title TEXT NOT NULL, salary INTEGER NOT NULL, manager_id INTEGER REFERENCES employees(id));
questions.solution: SELECT name, department, salary FROM employees ORDER BY department, salary DESC;

questions.title: Top 3
questions.question: Show the id and order_date of the 3 most recent orders, newest first.
questions.hint: Sort newest first, then keep only the first rows with LIMIT 3.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT id, order_date FROM orders ORDER BY order_date DESC LIMIT 3;

questions.title: Page two
questions.question: The product list shows 3 products per page, sorted by name A to Z. Show the names on page 2.
questions.hint: OFFSET skips rows before LIMIT starts counting. Page 2 skips the first 3.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT name FROM products ORDER BY name LIMIT 3 OFFSET 3;

questions.title: Count the rows
questions.question: How many orders has the shop received? Return a single number in a column called order_count.
questions.hint: COUNT(*) counts rows. Name the result with AS.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders;

questions.title: Count per group
questions.question: How many products are in each category? Show the category and a product_count column.
questions.hint: GROUP BY category makes one row per category. COUNT(*) then counts inside each group.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM products GROUP BY category;

questions.title: Spend per customer
questions.question: Show each customer_id and the total they have spent across all their orders, in a column called total_spent.
questions.hint: Group by customer_id and use SUM(total).
setupSql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT customer_id, SUM(total) AS total_spent FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id;

questions.title: Average salary
questions.question: HR wants the average salary in each department, rounded to the nearest whole number. Show department and avg_salary.
questions.hint: ROUND(AVG(salary)) rounds to a whole number. Group by department.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, department TEXT NOT NULL, title TEXT NOT NULL, salary INTEGER NOT NULL, manager_id INTEGER REFERENCES employees(id));
questions.solution: SELECT department, ROUND(AVG(salary)) AS avg_salary FROM employees GROUP BY department;

questions.title: Filter groups
questions.question: Which departments have more than 2 employees? Show department and employee_count.
questions.hint: WHERE filters rows before grouping. To filter on COUNT(*), use HAVING after GROUP BY.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, department TEXT NOT NULL, title TEXT NOT NULL, salary INTEGER NOT NULL, manager_id INTEGER REFERENCES employees(id));
questions.solution: SELECT department, COUNT(*) AS employee_count FROM employees GROUP BY department HAVING COUNT(*) > 2;

questions.title: Orders with names
questions.question: Orders only store a customer_id. Show each order id, the customer's name, and the order total.
questions.hint: JOIN customers ON customers.id = orders.customer_id links each order to its customer.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, city TEXT NOT NULL, country TEXT NOT NULL, signup_date TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT o.id, c.name, o.total FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id;

questions.title: Join, then filter
questions.question: Show the order id and customer name for every order placed by a customer in the UK.
questions.hint: Join first, then add a WHERE on the customers table: WHERE c.country = 'UK'.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, city TEXT NOT NULL, country TEXT NOT NULL, signup_date TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT o.id, c.name FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE c.country = 'UK';

questions.title: Include everyone
questions.question: Show every customer's name and how many orders they have placed, in a column called order_count. Customers with no orders must appear with 0.
questions.hint: An inner join drops customers without orders. Use LEFT JOIN, and COUNT(o.id) instead of COUNT(*) so the missing orders count as 0.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, city TEXT NOT NULL, country TEXT NOT NULL, signup_date TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS order_count FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name;

questions.title: Never ordered
questions.question: Sales wants to email customers who signed up but never ordered. Show the name of every customer with no orders at all.
questions.hint: LEFT JOIN orders, then keep the rows where the order side is empty: WHERE o.id IS NULL.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, city TEXT NOT NULL, country TEXT NOT NULL, signup_date TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT c.name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.id IS NULL;

questions.title: Follow the chain
questions.question: Which customers have bought at least one product from the Furniture category? Show each name once.
questions.hint: Chain the joins: customers → orders → order_items → products. Then filter on category and use DISTINCT.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, city TEXT NOT NULL, country TEXT NOT NULL, signup_date TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE order_items (order_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(id), product_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES products(id), quantity INTEGER NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT DISTINCT c.name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE p.category = 'Furniture';

questions.title: Above average
questions.question: Show the name and price of every product that costs more than the average product price.
questions.hint: A query in brackets can stand in for a value: WHERE price > (SELECT AVG(price) FROM products).
setupSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE price > (SELECT AVG(price) FROM products);

questions.title: Customers who cancelled
questions.question: Show the name of every customer who has at least one order with status 'cancelled'. Try it with a subquery instead of a join.
questions.hint: WHERE id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE status = 'cancelled').
setupSql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, city TEXT NOT NULL, country TEXT NOT NULL, signup_date TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE status = 'cancelled');

questions.title: Big spenders with a CTE
questions.question: Show the name and total spend (total_spent) of customers who have spent more than 400 in total. A CTE (WITH ... AS) keeps this readable.
questions.hint: WITH spend AS (SELECT customer_id, SUM(total) AS total_spent FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id) then join spend to customers and filter.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, city TEXT NOT NULL, country TEXT NOT NULL, signup_date TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: WITH spend AS (SELECT customer_id, SUM(total) AS total_spent FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT c.name, s.total_spent FROM spend s JOIN customers c ON c.id = s.customer_id WHERE s.total_spent > 400;

questions.title: Above their team average
questions.question: Show the name, department and salary of every employee who earns more than the average salary of their own department.
questions.hint: A correlated subquery can refer to the outer row: (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees e2 WHERE e2.department = e.department).
setupSql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, department TEXT NOT NULL, title TEXT NOT NULL, salary INTEGER NOT NULL, manager_id INTEGER REFERENCES employees(id));
questions.solution: SELECT e.name, e.department, e.salary FROM employees e WHERE e.salary > (SELECT AVG(e2.salary) FROM employees e2 WHERE e2.department = e.department);

questions.title: Rank within a category
questions.question: Show each product's category, name and price, plus a price_rank column: 1 for the most expensive product in its category, 2 for the next, and so on.
questions.hint: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY price DESC) restarts the count for each category.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT category, name, price, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY price DESC) AS price_rank FROM products;

questions.title: Running total
questions.question: Show each order's order_date and total, plus a running_total column that adds up all order totals up to and including that order. Sort by order_date, oldest first.
questions.hint: SUM(total) OVER (ORDER BY order_date) keeps a running sum instead of collapsing rows like GROUP BY.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT order_date, total, SUM(total) OVER (ORDER BY order_date) AS running_total FROM orders ORDER BY order_date;

questions.title: Top earner per team
questions.question: Show the highest-paid employee in each department: department, name and salary. The columns can be in any order.
questions.hint: Number the rows per department with ROW_NUMBER() in a CTE, then keep rows where the number is 1. You cannot filter a window function in WHERE directly.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, department TEXT NOT NULL, title TEXT NOT NULL, salary INTEGER NOT NULL, manager_id INTEGER REFERENCES employees(id));
questions.solution: WITH ranked AS (SELECT department, name, salary, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rn FROM employees) SELECT department, name, salary FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1;

questions.title: Join text together
questions.question: Show each customer's name and a location column that combines city and country, like 'Mumbai, India'.
questions.hint: || joins text in SQLite: city || ', ' || country.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, city TEXT NOT NULL, country TEXT NOT NULL, signup_date TEXT NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT name, city || ', ' || country AS location FROM customers;

questions.title: Shout the names
questions.question: Show every product name in capital letters as name_upper, followed by its category.
questions.hint: UPPER(name) converts text to capitals.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT UPPER(name) AS name_upper, category FROM products;

questions.title: Sale prices
questions.question: The shop is running a 10% off sale. Show each product name and its sale_price (price minus 10%), rounded to 2 decimal places.
questions.hint: price * 0.9 is the price after 10% off. Wrap it in ROUND(..., 2).
setupSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT name, ROUND(price * 0.9, 2) AS sale_price FROM products;

questions.title: Monthly pay
questions.question: Show each employee's name, yearly salary, and monthly_salary (salary divided by 12, rounded to a whole number).
questions.hint: Dividing two whole numbers drops the decimals in SQLite. Divide by 12.0, then ROUND.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, department TEXT NOT NULL, title TEXT NOT NULL, salary INTEGER NOT NULL, manager_id INTEGER REFERENCES employees(id));
questions.solution: SELECT name, salary, ROUND(salary / 12.0) AS monthly_salary FROM employees;

questions.title: Not delivered yet
questions.question: Show the id and status of every order that has not been delivered.
questions.hint: != (or <>) means not equal: WHERE status != 'delivered'.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT id, status FROM orders WHERE status != 'delivered';

questions.title: Two countries
questions.question: Show the name and country of every customer based in the UK or the USA.
questions.hint: IN checks against a list: WHERE country IN ('UK', 'USA').
setupSql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, city TEXT NOT NULL, country TEXT NOT NULL, signup_date TEXT NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT name, country FROM customers WHERE country IN ('UK', 'USA');

questions.title: Find the desks
questions.question: Show the name of every product with the word Desk anywhere in its name.
questions.hint: % matches any text, so LIKE '%Desk%' finds Desk anywhere.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%Desk%';

questions.title: Reachable customers
questions.question: Show the name and email of every customer who has an email address on file.
questions.hint: IS NOT NULL keeps rows where a value exists.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, city TEXT NOT NULL, country TEXT NOT NULL, signup_date TEXT NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT name, email FROM customers WHERE email IS NOT NULL;

questions.title: Either condition
questions.question: Show the name and price of products that are in the Stationery category or cost more than 250.
questions.hint: OR keeps a row when at least one condition is true.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE category = 'Stationery' OR price > 250;

questions.title: A to Z
questions.question: List every customer name in alphabetical order.
questions.hint: ORDER BY sorts text A to Z by default.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, city TEXT NOT NULL, country TEXT NOT NULL, signup_date TEXT NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT name FROM customers ORDER BY name;

questions.title: Earliest sign-ups
questions.question: Show the name and signup_date of every customer, earliest sign-up first.
questions.hint: Dates stored as YYYY-MM-DD text sort correctly with a plain ORDER BY.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, city TEXT NOT NULL, country TEXT NOT NULL, signup_date TEXT NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT name, signup_date FROM customers ORDER BY signup_date;

questions.title: Bargain bin
questions.question: Show the name and price of the 3 cheapest products, cheapest first.
questions.hint: Sort by price ascending, then LIMIT 3.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price LIMIT 3;

questions.title: Total revenue
questions.question: What is the combined value of all orders? Return one number in a column called total_revenue.
questions.hint: SUM(total) adds up a column.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT SUM(total) AS total_revenue FROM orders;

questions.title: Price range
questions.question: Show the lowest and the highest product price in one row, as min_price and max_price.
questions.hint: MIN and MAX can sit side by side in the same SELECT.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT MIN(price) AS min_price, MAX(price) AS max_price FROM products;

questions.title: Orders by status
questions.question: How many orders are in each status? Show status and order_count.
questions.hint: GROUP BY status, then COUNT(*).
setupSql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders GROUP BY status;

questions.title: Customers per country
questions.question: How many customers does the shop have in each country? Show country and customer_count.
questions.hint: One group per country, counted with COUNT(*).
setupSql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, city TEXT NOT NULL, country TEXT NOT NULL, signup_date TEXT NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT country, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM customers GROUP BY country;

questions.title: What was in each order
questions.question: For every row in order_items, show the order_id, the product name and the quantity.
questions.hint: order_items.product_id matches products.id.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE order_items (order_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(id), product_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES products(id), quantity INTEGER NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT oi.order_id, p.name, oi.quantity FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id;

questions.title: Ratings with names
questions.question: Show every review as the product name and its rating.
questions.hint: Join reviews to products on reviews.product_id = products.id.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);

CREATE TABLE reviews (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, product_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES products(id), customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), rating INTEGER NOT NULL, review_date TEXT NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT p.name, r.rating FROM reviews r JOIN products p ON p.id = r.product_id;

questions.title: The priciest item
questions.question: Show the name of the most expensive product. Use a subquery to find the highest price.
questions.hint: WHERE price = (SELECT MAX(price) FROM products).
setupSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT name FROM products WHERE price = (SELECT MAX(price) FROM products);

questions.title: Number the catalogue
questions.question: Show each product name and price, plus a position column: 1 for the most expensive product, 2 for the next, and so on.
questions.hint: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY price DESC).
setupSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT name, price, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY price DESC) AS position FROM products;

questions.title: Price tiers
questions.question: Show each product's name, price and a tier column: 'premium' when the price is 200 or more, otherwise 'standard'.
questions.hint: CASE WHEN price >= 200 THEN 'premium' ELSE 'standard' END.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT name, price, CASE WHEN price >= 200 THEN 'premium' ELSE 'standard' END AS tier FROM products;

questions.title: Fill the gaps
questions.question: Show each customer's name and a contact column with their email, or the text 'no email' when it is missing.
questions.hint: COALESCE(email, 'no email') returns the first value that is not NULL.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, city TEXT NOT NULL, country TEXT NOT NULL, signup_date TEXT NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT name, COALESCE(email, 'no email') AS contact FROM customers;

questions.title: April orders
questions.question: Show the id and order_date of every order placed in April 2024.
questions.hint: Either BETWEEN '2024-04-01' AND '2024-04-30', or order_date LIKE '2024-04%'.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT id, order_date FROM orders WHERE order_date BETWEEN '2024-04-01' AND '2024-04-30';

questions.title: Brackets matter
questions.question: Show the id, status and total of orders worth more than 200 whose status is either 'delivered' or 'shipped'.
questions.hint: AND is evaluated before OR. Put the two statuses in brackets: total > 200 AND (status = ... OR status = ...).
setupSql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT id, status, total FROM orders WHERE total > 200 AND (status = 'delivered' OR status = 'shipped');

questions.title: Early adopters
questions.question: Show the name and country of customers who signed up between 1 January and 30 June 2023 (inclusive) and live in India or the UK.
questions.hint: Combine a BETWEEN on signup_date with an IN on country, joined by AND.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, city TEXT NOT NULL, country TEXT NOT NULL, signup_date TEXT NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT name, country FROM customers WHERE signup_date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-06-30' AND country IN ('India', 'UK');

questions.title: Grouped and sorted
questions.question: Show the id, status and total of every order. Sort by status A to Z, and within each status put the largest total first.
questions.hint: ORDER BY status, total DESC.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT id, status, total FROM orders ORDER BY status, total DESC;

questions.title: Missing values last
questions.question: Show each customer name and email, sorted by email A to Z with missing emails at the end. Break ties by name A to Z.
questions.hint: SQLite puts NULL first. ORDER BY email IS NULL, email, name pushes NULLs to the bottom (or use NULLS LAST).
setupSql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, city TEXT NOT NULL, country TEXT NOT NULL, signup_date TEXT NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT name, email FROM customers ORDER BY email IS NULL, email, name;

questions.title: The middle of the table
questions.question: Show the name and salary of the employees with the 4th, 5th and 6th highest salaries, highest first.
questions.hint: Sort by salary descending, skip 3 rows with OFFSET 3, then take 3 with LIMIT 3.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, department TEXT NOT NULL, title TEXT NOT NULL, salary INTEGER NOT NULL, manager_id INTEGER REFERENCES employees(id));
questions.solution: SELECT name, salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 3 OFFSET 3;

questions.title: Status summary
questions.question: For each order status, show the status, the number of orders (order_count) and the average order total rounded to 2 decimals (avg_total).
questions.hint: You can use several aggregates in one grouped query: COUNT(*), ROUND(AVG(total), 2).
setupSql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS order_count, ROUND(AVG(total), 2) AS avg_total FROM orders GROUP BY status;

questions.title: Two-level grouping
questions.question: Count employees for every combination of department and title. Show department, title and employee_count.
questions.hint: GROUP BY department, title makes one group per combination.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, department TEXT NOT NULL, title TEXT NOT NULL, salary INTEGER NOT NULL, manager_id INTEGER REFERENCES employees(id));
questions.solution: SELECT department, title, COUNT(*) AS employee_count FROM employees GROUP BY department, title;

questions.title: Monthly revenue
questions.question: Show revenue per month: month (like 2024-01) and revenue (sum of order totals), oldest month first. Leave out cancelled orders.
questions.hint: substr(order_date, 1, 7) turns '2024-01-05' into '2024-01'. Filter with WHERE before grouping.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT substr(order_date, 1, 7) AS month, SUM(total) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE status != 'cancelled' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month;

questions.title: Valuable customers
questions.question: Which customers have spent more than 300 on orders that were not cancelled? Show customer_id and total_spent.
questions.hint: WHERE removes cancelled orders first, then HAVING SUM(total) > 300 filters the groups.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT customer_id, SUM(total) AS total_spent FROM orders WHERE status != 'cancelled' GROUP BY customer_id HAVING SUM(total) > 300;

questions.title: Units by category
questions.question: Show each product category and the total number of units sold (units_sold).
questions.hint: Join order_items to products, group by category, and SUM(quantity).
setupSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE order_items (order_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(id), product_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES products(id), quantity INTEGER NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS units_sold FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.category;

questions.title: Average rating
questions.question: Show the name of every product that has reviews, with its average rating rounded to 1 decimal place (avg_rating).
questions.hint: Join reviews to products, group by product, and use ROUND(AVG(rating), 1).
setupSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);

CREATE TABLE reviews (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, product_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES products(id), customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), rating INTEGER NOT NULL, review_date TEXT NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT p.name, ROUND(AVG(r.rating), 1) AS avg_rating FROM reviews r JOIN products p ON p.id = r.product_id GROUP BY p.id, p.name;

questions.title: No reviews yet
questions.question: Which products have never been reviewed? Show their names.
questions.hint: LEFT JOIN reviews, then keep rows where r.id IS NULL.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);

CREATE TABLE reviews (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, product_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES products(id), customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), rating INTEGER NOT NULL, review_date TEXT NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT p.name FROM products p LEFT JOIN reviews r ON r.product_id = p.id WHERE r.id IS NULL;

questions.title: Who is the boss?
questions.question: Show every employee who has a manager, as two columns: employee (their name) and manager (their manager's name).
questions.hint: Join employees to itself: JOIN employees m ON m.id = e.manager_id.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, department TEXT NOT NULL, title TEXT NOT NULL, salary INTEGER NOT NULL, manager_id INTEGER REFERENCES employees(id));
questions.solution: SELECT e.name AS employee, m.name AS manager FROM employees e JOIN employees m ON m.id = e.manager_id;

questions.title: Money received
questions.question: Show each customer who has made a payment, with their name and the total amount they have paid (amount_paid).
questions.hint: Payments belong to orders, and orders belong to customers. Join payments → orders → customers, then group.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, city TEXT NOT NULL, country TEXT NOT NULL, signup_date TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE payments (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, order_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(id), paid_at TEXT NOT NULL, method TEXT NOT NULL, amount REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT c.name, SUM(pay.amount) AS amount_paid FROM payments pay JOIN orders o ON o.id = pay.order_id JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name;

questions.title: Silent customers
questions.question: Show the name of every customer who has never written a review. Use NOT IN with a subquery.
questions.hint: WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT customer_id FROM reviews).
setupSql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, city TEXT NOT NULL, country TEXT NOT NULL, signup_date TEXT NOT NULL);

CREATE TABLE reviews (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, product_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES products(id), customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), rating INTEGER NOT NULL, review_date TEXT NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT customer_id FROM reviews);

questions.title: Still on the way
questions.question: Show the name of every product that is part of an order that is 'shipped' or 'pending'. Use EXISTS.
questions.hint: EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON ... WHERE oi.product_id = p.id AND o.status IN (...)).
setupSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE order_items (order_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(id), product_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES products(id), quantity INTEGER NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT p.name FROM products p WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id WHERE oi.product_id = p.id AND o.status IN ('shipped', 'pending'));

questions.title: Distance from average
questions.question: Show each product's name, price, and diff_from_avg: how far its price is above (positive) or below (negative) the average product price, rounded to 2 decimals.
questions.hint: A scalar subquery works inside SELECT too: price - (SELECT AVG(price) FROM products).
setupSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT name, price, ROUND(price - (SELECT AVG(price) FROM products), 2) AS diff_from_avg FROM products;

questions.title: Basket size
questions.question: On average, how many units does an order contain? Return one number, avg_items_per_order. Use a subquery in FROM that totals the quantity per order.
questions.hint: SELECT AVG(units) FROM (SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity) AS units FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id).
setupSql: CREATE TABLE order_items (order_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(id), product_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES products(id), quantity INTEGER NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT AVG(units) AS avg_items_per_order FROM (SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity) AS units FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id);

questions.title: Total on every row
questions.question: Show each order id and total, plus grand_total: the sum of all order totals, repeated on every row.
questions.hint: SUM(total) OVER () with empty brackets uses all rows as the window.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT id, total, SUM(total) OVER () AS grand_total FROM orders;

questions.title: Team size
questions.question: Show each employee's name and department, plus dept_size: how many people work in that department. Keep one row per employee.
questions.hint: COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY department).
setupSql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, department TEXT NOT NULL, title TEXT NOT NULL, salary INTEGER NOT NULL, manager_id INTEGER REFERENCES employees(id));
questions.solution: SELECT name, department, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY department) AS dept_size FROM employees;

questions.title: Previous order
questions.question: For each order, show id, order_date and previous_order_date: the date of the order placed just before it (across all customers).
questions.hint: LAG(order_date) OVER (ORDER BY order_date).
setupSql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT id, order_date, LAG(order_date) OVER (ORDER BY order_date) AS previous_order_date FROM orders;

questions.title: Best sellers with ties
questions.question: Show each product name, its total units_sold, and a sales_rank where 1 is the best seller. Products with the same units share a rank, and the next rank is skipped (like 1, 2, 2, 4).
questions.hint: Total the units per product in a CTE, then use RANK() OVER (ORDER BY units_sold DESC).
setupSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE order_items (order_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(id), product_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES products(id), quantity INTEGER NOT NULL);
questions.solution: WITH units AS (SELECT p.name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS units_sold FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON oi.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.id, p.name) SELECT name, units_sold, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY units_sold DESC) AS sales_rank FROM units;

questions.title: Order size buckets
questions.question: Show each order's id, total and size: 'small' under 50, 'medium' from 50 to 300 inclusive, and 'large' above 300.
questions.hint: CASE checks conditions in order and stops at the first match, so start with the smallest bucket.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT id, total, CASE WHEN total < 50 THEN 'small' WHEN total <= 300 THEN 'medium' ELSE 'large' END AS size FROM orders;

questions.title: The NULL trap
questions.question: Show the name of every customer whose email does not end in '@example.com'. Customers with no email count too.
questions.hint: NOT LIKE on a NULL gives NULL, not true, so those rows vanish. Add OR email IS NULL.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, city TEXT NOT NULL, country TEXT NOT NULL, signup_date TEXT NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE email NOT LIKE '%@example.com' OR email IS NULL;

questions.title: The last 30 days
questions.question: Show the id and order_date of orders placed in the 30 days up to and including the most recent order date.
questions.hint: date(x, '-30 days') shifts a date. Find the latest date with (SELECT MAX(order_date) FROM orders).
setupSql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT id, order_date FROM orders WHERE order_date >= date((SELECT MAX(order_date) FROM orders), '-30 days');

questions.title: Workflow order
questions.question: Show the id and status of every order, sorted in workflow order: pending, then shipped, then delivered, then cancelled. Within each status, newest order first.
questions.hint: ORDER BY a CASE that turns each status into a number, then order_date DESC.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT id, status FROM orders ORDER BY CASE status WHEN 'pending' THEN 1 WHEN 'shipped' THEN 2 WHEN 'delivered' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END, order_date DESC;

questions.title: Most loyal customers
questions.question: Show the 2 customers who placed the most orders: name and order_count, most orders first. Break ties by name A to Z.
questions.hint: Join, group by customer, ORDER BY order_count DESC, name, then LIMIT 2.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, city TEXT NOT NULL, country TEXT NOT NULL, signup_date TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name ORDER BY order_count DESC, c.name LIMIT 2;

questions.title: Counting with conditions
questions.question: For each customer_id in orders, show total_orders and delivered_orders (how many of them were delivered) in one query.
questions.hint: SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'delivered' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) counts only matching rows.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS total_orders, SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'delivered' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS delivered_orders FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id;

questions.title: Big, pricey categories
questions.question: Which categories have more than 2 products and an average price above 100? Show category, product_count and avg_price rounded to 2 decimals.
questions.hint: HAVING can combine conditions with AND: HAVING COUNT(*) > 2 AND AVG(price) > 100.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS product_count, ROUND(AVG(price), 2) AS avg_price FROM products GROUP BY category HAVING COUNT(*) > 2 AND AVG(price) > 100;

questions.title: Share of units
questions.question: Show each category and pct_of_units: its share of all units sold as a percentage, rounded to 1 decimal place.
questions.hint: Divide each group's SUM(quantity) by the overall total from a subquery. Multiply by 100.0 first to avoid whole-number division.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE order_items (order_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(id), product_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES products(id), quantity INTEGER NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT p.category, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(oi.quantity) / (SELECT SUM(quantity) FROM order_items), 1) AS pct_of_units FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.category;

questions.title: Customer lifespan
questions.question: For each customer_id in orders, show first_order (earliest date), last_order (latest date) and days_between: the whole number of days between them.
questions.hint: julianday(date) turns a date into a number of days. CAST(julianday(MAX(order_date)) - julianday(MIN(order_date)) AS INTEGER).
setupSql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT customer_id, MIN(order_date) AS first_order, MAX(order_date) AS last_order, CAST(julianday(MAX(order_date)) - julianday(MIN(order_date)) AS INTEGER) AS days_between FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id;

questions.title: Revenue by country
questions.question: Show delivered revenue per country: country and revenue (sum of delivered order totals), highest revenue first.
questions.hint: Join orders to customers, filter status = 'delivered', group by country, then sort.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, city TEXT NOT NULL, country TEXT NOT NULL, signup_date TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT c.country, SUM(o.total) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY c.country ORDER BY revenue DESC;

questions.title: Filter in the ON
questions.question: Show every customer's name and how many delivered orders they have (delivered_orders). Customers with none must appear with 0.
questions.hint: Filtering status in WHERE removes customers without delivered orders. Put it in the join instead: LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id AND o.status = 'delivered'.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, city TEXT NOT NULL, country TEXT NOT NULL, signup_date TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS delivered_orders FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id AND o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY c.id, c.name;

questions.title: Not fully paid
questions.question: Find orders that have not been fully paid. Show id, total and amount_paid (0 if nothing was paid). Leave out cancelled orders.
questions.hint: LEFT JOIN payments, group by order, use COALESCE(SUM(amount), 0), and HAVING to keep orders where paid < total. Some orders are paid in two parts.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE payments (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, order_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(id), paid_at TEXT NOT NULL, method TEXT NOT NULL, amount REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT o.id, o.total, COALESCE(SUM(p.amount), 0) AS amount_paid FROM orders o LEFT JOIN payments p ON p.order_id = o.id WHERE o.status != 'cancelled' GROUP BY o.id, o.total HAVING COALESCE(SUM(p.amount), 0) < o.total;

questions.title: Suspicious reviews
questions.question: Find reviews written by customers who never ordered the product they reviewed. Show the customer name and the product name.
questions.hint: Join reviews to customers and products, then use NOT EXISTS with orders joined to order_items for the same customer and product.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, city TEXT NOT NULL, country TEXT NOT NULL, signup_date TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE order_items (order_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(id), product_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES products(id), quantity INTEGER NOT NULL);

CREATE TABLE reviews (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, product_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES products(id), customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), rating INTEGER NOT NULL, review_date TEXT NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT c.name AS customer, p.name AS product FROM reviews r JOIN customers c ON c.id = r.customer_id JOIN products p ON p.id = r.product_id WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id WHERE o.customer_id = r.customer_id AND oi.product_id = r.product_id);

questions.title: Pay gaps within teams
questions.question: List every pair of employees in the same department where the first earns more than the second. Show higher_paid, lower_paid and department.
questions.hint: Join employees to itself on department, and keep pairs where a.salary > b.salary.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, department TEXT NOT NULL, title TEXT NOT NULL, salary INTEGER NOT NULL, manager_id INTEGER REFERENCES employees(id));
questions.solution: SELECT a.name AS higher_paid, b.name AS lower_paid, a.department FROM employees a JOIN employees b ON a.department = b.department AND a.salary > b.salary;

questions.title: Perfect delivery record
questions.question: Show the name of every customer who has placed at least one order and whose orders were all delivered.
questions.hint: Two checks: the customer appears in orders, and NOT EXISTS an order of theirs with status != 'delivered'.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, city TEXT NOT NULL, country TEXT NOT NULL, signup_date TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT c.name FROM customers c WHERE c.id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id AND o.status != 'delivered');

questions.title: Bigger than usual
questions.question: Show the id, customer_id and total of every order that is larger than that customer's own average order total.
questions.hint: Correlated subquery: total > (SELECT AVG(o2.total) FROM orders o2 WHERE o2.customer_id = o.customer_id).
setupSql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT o.id, o.customer_id, o.total FROM orders o WHERE o.total > (SELECT AVG(o2.total) FROM orders o2 WHERE o2.customer_id = o.customer_id);

questions.title: Top earner per category
questions.question: Show the product with the highest revenue (units sold × price) in each category: category, name and revenue. Do it without window functions.
questions.hint: Build revenue per product in a CTE, then keep rows whose revenue equals the MAX revenue for their category (a correlated subquery on the CTE).
setupSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE order_items (order_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(id), product_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES products(id), quantity INTEGER NOT NULL);
questions.solution: WITH rev AS (SELECT p.category, p.name, SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) AS revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON oi.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.id, p.category, p.name) SELECT category, name, revenue FROM rev r WHERE revenue = (SELECT MAX(revenue) FROM rev r2 WHERE r2.category = r.category);

questions.title: Above-average buyers
questions.question: Show the name and order_count of customers who placed more orders than the average customer who has ordered.
questions.hint: HAVING COUNT(*) > (SELECT AVG(cnt) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id)).
setupSql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, city TEXT NOT NULL, country TEXT NOT NULL, signup_date TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name HAVING COUNT(*) > (SELECT AVG(cnt) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id));

questions.title: Org chart levels
questions.question: Show every employee's name and their level in the org chart: 1 for people with no manager, 2 for their direct reports, 3 for the next layer, and so on.
questions.hint: WITH RECURSIVE: start with managers (manager_id IS NULL, level 1), then repeatedly join employees whose manager_id is in the previous layer, adding 1.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, department TEXT NOT NULL, title TEXT NOT NULL, salary INTEGER NOT NULL, manager_id INTEGER REFERENCES employees(id));
questions.solution: WITH RECURSIVE chain AS (SELECT id, name, 1 AS level FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT e.id, e.name, c.level + 1 FROM employees e JOIN chain c ON e.manager_id = c.id) SELECT name, level FROM chain;

questions.title: Running total per customer
questions.question: Show customer_id, order_date, total and running_total, where the running total restarts for each customer. Sort by customer_id, then order_date.
questions.hint: SUM(total) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date).
setupSql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT customer_id, order_date, total, SUM(total) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date) AS running_total FROM orders ORDER BY customer_id, order_date;

questions.title: Moving average
questions.question: Show each order_date and total with moving_avg: the average of this order and the two before it (by date), rounded to 2 decimals. Sort by order_date.
questions.hint: A frame limits the window: AVG(total) OVER (ORDER BY order_date ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW).
setupSql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT order_date, total, ROUND(AVG(total) OVER (ORDER BY order_date ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS moving_avg FROM orders ORDER BY order_date;

questions.title: Share of team payroll
questions.question: Show each employee's name, department, salary and pct_of_dept: their share of the department's total salary as a percentage, rounded to 1 decimal.
questions.hint: 100.0 * salary / SUM(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department).
setupSql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, department TEXT NOT NULL, title TEXT NOT NULL, salary INTEGER NOT NULL, manager_id INTEGER REFERENCES employees(id));
questions.solution: SELECT name, department, salary, ROUND(100.0 * salary / SUM(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department), 1) AS pct_of_dept FROM employees;

questions.title: First purchase
questions.question: Show each customer's first order: customer name, order id and order_date. Only customers who have ordered.
questions.hint: Number each customer's orders by date with ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date), then keep number 1.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, city TEXT NOT NULL, country TEXT NOT NULL, signup_date TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: WITH numbered AS (SELECT o.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date) AS rn FROM orders o) SELECT c.name, n.id, n.order_date FROM numbered n JOIN customers c ON c.id = n.customer_id WHERE n.rn = 1;

questions.title: Split into halves
questions.question: Split the products into two equal groups by price. Show name, price and price_half: 1 for the more expensive half, 2 for the cheaper half.
questions.hint: NTILE(2) OVER (ORDER BY price DESC) divides the rows into 2 buckets.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT name, price, NTILE(2) OVER (ORDER BY price DESC) AS price_half FROM products;

questions.title: Time between orders
questions.question: For each order, show id, customer_id, order_date and days_since_previous: whole days since the same customer's previous order (NULL for their first order).
questions.hint: LAG(order_date) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date), then subtract with julianday and CAST to INTEGER.
setupSql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL);
questions.solution: SELECT id, customer_id, order_date, CAST(julianday(order_date) - julianday(LAG(order_date) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date)) AS INTEGER) AS days_since_previous FROM orders;
